reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset and Brown distinguish numbering itself, which God commanded through Moses, from David's sin of numbering without divine sanction and out of pride.

discrepancy.note: Wellhausen calls census-taking itself repugnant to early Israel, noting 2 Samuel 24 sits uneasily beside the repeated enumerations elsewhere credited to David.

quotes.text: surveys and censuses were repugnant in the extreme. In spite of 2Samuel xxiv., we are told that under David enumerations both of the spiritual and of the secular tribes were made again and again
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885), ch. VI.III, on 2 Samuel 24:1 and Numbers 1:2.

sides.snippet: Take a census of all the congregation of the children of Israel, by their families, by their fathers' houses, according to the number of the names, every male, one by one;

sides.snippet: Again the anger of Yahweh was kindled against Israel, and he moved David against them, saying, Go, number Israel and Judah.
